Gallery Walk QR Codes

Turn a list of student work links into a printable set of QR codes for a gallery walk — nothing leaves your browser

Student work entries
StationName / titleLink or text
Fills in the name column only — add each student's link or text after.

Example: Ava R.  docs.google.com/document/d/abc123
Also works with plain commas: Marco T., drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz

A link missing "https://" (like "docs.google.com/...") gets it added automatically. Anything that doesn't look like a link or address is encoded as plain text as-is — handy for pointing at instructions instead of a URL. If the work isn't online at all, click "Use multi-line prompt / rubric text" on a row to write out the prompt or rubric — it gets printed right on the card as well as encoded in the code.
Print layout
The reference sheet is just your own lookup list (name → link) — there's nothing secret on it, unlike an answer key, so it's fine to keep with the QR pages if that's handy.
Peer feedback slips
Slips don't need a link or QR code — a named entry with no link still gets a station slip, for work that's on paper or on display in the room.

Walking order & route cards
Spread students or groups across different starting stations so the whole class doesn't bottleneck at Station 1 — everyone still visits every station, just starting from a different spot and rotating forward from there.
No names loaded yet.
Each route card's number of stops matches "Number of rotations" in the timer above, so the printed route always matches how many times the timer will call a rotation.
Collected feedback (optional)
After the walk, jot down or paste what came back on the slips for any station — one comment per line — then print a take-home packet per student showing what their classmates said.
